people-whove-lived-on-both-sides-unvarni.headline: People Who've Lived On Both Sides - Unvarnished Life Stories
people-whove-lived-on-both-sides-unvarni.author: Michael Benest FRSA FACQP
people-whove-lived-on-both-sides-unvarni.core: Posted in last 7 days People Who've Lived On Both Sides - Unvarnished Life Stories LIVED ON BOTH SIDES. Good people. Bad decisions. Great stories. I've worked in kitchens, on building sites, in boardrooms and in galleries. I've spent much of my life around people who don't fit neatly into boxes. Chefs. Criminals. Artists. Bikers. Entrepreneurs. Millionaires. Misfits. People who've made fortunes. Lost everything. Gone to prison. Built empires. Got it spectacularly wrong. Started again. Some of the best people I've met have made terrible decisions. Some of the worst have impeccable CVs. Funny old world. I want the stories that don't make it onto LinkedIn. The uncomfortable ones. The hilarious ones. The ones people have spent years trying to forget. No motivational speeches. No rehearsed success stories. No pretending life is one long upward trajectory. Just proper conversations with people who've actually lived. Recording in Jersey, Britain, Canada and wherever else I find someone with a story worth telling. I'm looking for guests. You don't need to be famous, rich or particularly respectable. You need a story worth hearing and the nerve to tell it. Who deserves a microphone but has never been handed one? Message me. Nominate yourself. Or point them my way. To the 10,000 of you who've followed this far, thank you. Now I want to hear from you. LIVED ON BOTH SIDES. March 2027. 🎙️

employers-who-trialed-period-leave-and-l.core: Posted in last 7 days Employers Who Trialed Period Leave & Lactation Spaces - Results Don't get me wrong, I like a little cake during work hours. Or free lunch. I would not say no. However, I would also like to know where a new mother is supposed to pump at work when the only available room is a toilet. We spend a lot of time telling women to grow, lead and believe in themselves. Whole conferences on them. And that's all good and all... But what are we doing about the conditions they have to live and work in? I want to hear from the employer who asked women what they needed, tried a new policy and can tell us what happened. Period leave, mental health days, a properly equipped space for breastfeeding mothers. How did you get it approved? Did people use it? What would you change? Or how about supporting women's mental and physical health without giving them a discount for..diet candy. Or is that so 2020? What's the latest trend these days? I also want to hear about the questions women are still struggling to get straight answers to. What does the science say about health and nutrition during menstruation or perimenopause? What do you do when an interviewer assumes motherhood makes you less committed? Is there technology that genuinely helps you focus, stay organised, or educate you about your body without selling your data? And sometimes the question comes before any of that: how do you plan a career when you are worried about getting home to a decent meal? We’re working on something connected to the #WomenBuildingCyprus project (can't reveal any details yet). I don’t want to fill a stage with answers to questions nobody asked or care for. So tell me: what question do you keep searching for an answer to? Or have you built something, changed a workplace practice or found an approach that other women should know about? Comments and messages are both welcome. I would love to hear the specifics, including what didn’t work. (Photo: Let's stop putting our needs in the second lane.) #cyprus #women #mentalhealth #fitness #health #motherhood #body #career #founders #entrepreneurs #tech #science

gen-z-creators-and-young-professionals-r.headline: Gen Z Creators & Young Professionals - Rethinking Career Paths
gen-z-creators-and-young-professionals-r.author: Rana Shehroze Ahmed Khan
gen-z-creators-and-young-professionals-r.core: Posted in last 7 days Gen Z Creators & Young Professionals - Rethinking Career Paths Gen Z give up nahi karti ya bas apna raasta khud banana chahti hai? Humne success ka ek roadmap bana rakha hai. Matric karo. College jao. Degree lo. Job hasil karo. Aur agar koi is raaste se hat kar kuch different karna chahe, toh humare paas labels ready hain. Confused hai. Serious nahi hai. Isay abhi life ka pata nahi. Lekin ek sawaal hai, Kya hum waqai Gen Z ko samajhne ki koshish kar rahe hain, ya sirf unhein apni definition of success ke mutabiq judge kar rahe hain? I've always believed that learning isn't limited to a degree, a job title, or a particular field. My own journey has taken me through computer science, business, academia, entrepreneurship, and now training and strategic partnerships, and one thing I've realised is that sometimes, you discover what you're capable of only when you allow yourself to explore beyond what you already know. That doesn't mean degrees don't matter or that every unconventional path is the right one. It simply means we shouldn't confuse having a different path with having no direction. This is exactly the kind of conversation I wanted to bring to EmpowerMe Talks. In this episode, I sat down with Syed Aarian Ali, a young content strategist, to explore the Gen Z mindset, unconventional careers, content creation, and the courage to build something of your own. One question sits at the heart of this conversation What happens when you stop being a consumer of ideas and start becoming a creator?Because watching others build their dreams is one thing, starting with what you have, learning along the way, putting your work out there, and building your own identity is another. We discussed: → Why Gen Z is questioning traditional career paths → The pressure of parents, society, and external validation → From consuming content to creating opportunities (And Many More) I don't think the answer is to abandon conventional paths. The answer is to give people the skills, confidence, and freedom to make informed choices about their own paths. Maybe some will become engineers. Some will become creators. Some will build businesses. And some will combine completely different fields to create something that doesn't even exist yet. Why should we expect everyone to follow the same script? Syed Aarian Ali, Thank you for joining me for this conversation and sharing your perspective. I hope it encourages more young people to question assumptions, take initiative, and explore what they're capable of building. 🎙️ Watch the full episode of EmpowerMe Talks on YouTube. (Link is the comments) If you're a student, young professional, aspiring creator, or someone figuring out your next move, this conversation is for you. And if you have a story, experience, or expertise that could help others learn something meaningful, I'd love to hear from you. Want to be a guest on EmpowerMe Talks?
